notes: Create each file from the service-owned credential workflow; do not copy personal CLI credential directories.
Set CYRENE_HF_ENABLED=false for a GitHub-only bootstrap/staging run; no Hugging Face secret, token, binding, catalog, or profile is required in that mode.

When CYRENE_HF_ENABLED=true, provide the private device-OAuth bootstrap file and the HF-only mTLS/HMAC files listed above; never migrate the old personal OAuth token file or put HF tokens in Exchange or ordinary environment variables.

The Hugging Face OAuth bootstrap file is mounted read-only into Account Center only when the HF Compose overlay is selected; retain it owner-only for runtime restart and reauthentication until a persisted-config rollout removes the file ref and mount.
Provision `codebuddy/` as a separate owner-only service login directory beneath the private artifact `secrets/`; never copy or mount a personal `~/.codebuddy` tree.
Files must be regular non-symlinks with mode 0400; Postgres server TLS files belong to UID 999, and Postgres admin password is readable by the root entrypoint only.

Directory admin URL is mounted only into one-shot schema migration and role bootstrap. Operator URL is mounted only into role bootstrap and the explicit one-shot maintainer profile. Runtime reader URL is mounted into role bootstrap and the connector-authority runtime only.
All other service secrets belong to UID 10001. Public CA certificate files remain private config files and are mounted read-only.

Exchange and Account Center use the same 32-byte hex or base64 `account-center-exchange-hmac-key` value for their pairwise signed-caller contract. Navigator-Exchange and Teams-Navigator each use separate keys.
Use a distinct pairwise HMAC key for Teams-Navigator, Navigator-Exchange, Exchange-Account-Center, and Exchange-cloud-management boundaries; never reuse one boundary key elsewhere.

The internal-service-root-ca is public certificate data used to verify private Exchange and Navigator Persistence HTTPS endpoints; exchange-tls-cert/key and navigator-persistence-tls-cert/key are listener-only leaves with matching DNS SANs.

The computer-runtime-proxy-server-cert/key pair belongs only to the Caddy mTLS sidecar and must have DNS SAN computer-runtime-proxy; the runner itself receives no TLS, HMAC, model, or connector credentials.
DirectPluginRuntime server certificates use SANs for their Compose DNS names; the plugin client-CA bundle trusts only Exchange and the service-specific health probe identities.
The Authority signing seed stays mounted only into the Authority workload. Exchange receives the generated public-only keyring.
